correctness.rationale: For all positive n, multiplicativity reduces s_{-3}(n) to local factors f_p(e)=sum_{j=0}^e(-p^{-3})^j. For p>=11, an exact five-prime exceptional certificate and Nagura’s prime interval theorem for p>=29 prove u_p=-log(1-p^-3)<=sum_{q>p}u_q; the subsum interval lemma therefore fills the closure [T,1]. Exact inequalities T f_p(2)<=f_p(1) for p=3,5,7 and T f_2(4)<=f_2(3) reduce arbitrary prime powers to 135 rational scales. Independently computed all 135, merged them using rigorous rational two-sided bounds from floor(10^18/k^3) through k=100000 and an analytic tail, and verified ALL 19 submitted rational endpoint pairs, all 18 strict gaps and every overlap. Closest certified separation >0.0000326 and overlap >0.0002716. This proves 19 components given the stated standard prime-gap and subsum lemmas; the finite rational certificate alone is not the infinite tail proof.
